prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Reloading a provider from storage never restores `token_expiry_time` (only tokens/client_info are reloaded in `_initialize`). `is_token_valid()` therefore treats an expired stored access token as still valid, the proactive-refresh branch is skipped, and the first real request gets a 401 that the client answers with a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. Both PRs' own descriptions/comments name this exact root cause. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Reloading a provider from storage never restores `token_expiry_time` (only tokens/client_info are reloaded in `_initialize`). `is_token_valid()` therefore treats an expired stored access token as still valid, the proactive-refresh branch is skipped, and the first real request gets a 401 that the client answers with a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. Both PRs' own descriptions/comments name this exact root cause. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes the root cause directly and minimally: `_initialize()` now calls `update_token_expiry()` when loading stored tokens (4-line change), restoring correct behavior for the existing proactive is_token_valid()/refresh path, and ships a new `expired_tokens` fixture for regression coverage. #2875 only patches the downstream symptom by inserting an extra refresh-then-retry round trip inside the 401 handler ('Step 3.5'), leaving token_expiry_time itself unset and is_token_valid() still wrong, while adding more branching/state to async_auth_flow.

prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the failure path of _handle_reconnection() for the SSE reconnection logic in streamable_http.py: when reconnection to resume the stream ultimately fails, the waiting caller currently gets nothing (a silent hang) or an opaque/wrong exception instead of a clear, actionable error. #2395 fixes this by detecting the 'max attempts exceeded' branch and pushing an explicit JSONRPCError (matched to the original request id) through read_stream_writer. #3098 fixes it by adding a recursive _unwrap_exception() helper that digs a StreamableHTTPError out of anyio's ExceptionGroup wrapping so the correct exception type propagates on reconnection failure. Same trigger (reconnection failing) and same goal (caller must learn about the failure instead of hanging/getting a useless error) via two different mechanisms (in-band JSON-RPC error vs. raised exception). (2 PRs)

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both change how the write-side memory-object-stream in stdio_server() is sized, targeting the same underlying limitation: an unbuffered (maxsize=0) write_stream forces the stdout writer to be lockstep with producers, which can block/deadlock a handler trying to enqueue a final response while an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification) is still being flushed to stdout. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both change how the write-side memory-object-stream in stdio_server() is sized, targeting the same underlying limitation: an unbuffered (maxsize=0) write_stream forces the stdout writer to be lockstep with producers, which can block/deadlock a handler trying to enqueue a final response while an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification) is still being flushed to stdout. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2654 fixes the blocking scenario by default (write buffer 0->1) with no API change required, and ships a dedicated regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces a handler queuing a response while a progress notification is still being written. #2215 only adds opt-in read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters defaulting to 0, so out-of-the-box behavior is unchanged and the deadlock persists unless every caller remembers to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1. #2215's diff also still calls anyio.create_memory_object_stream directly rather than the create_context_streams helper that appears in both #2552 and #2654's base, indicating it was branched off an older revision of stdio.py and will need to be rebased against the already-merged newline fix, creating avoidable conflict.

prs.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result

They cannot both be applied as intended: whichever merges second either re-breaks the other's fix or sits as dead code on top of it. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2962's test/comment cites SEP-1577 and issue #2960 as the spec basis: tool_result blocks must be preceded by tool_use, but tool_use carries no requirement to be followed by tool_result, so no-raise is the spec-conformant behavior. #3053 only improves the error message while preserving the raise, which contradicts that cited spec requirement, so it should be closed in favor of #2962.

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py where WWW-Authenticate header parsing does naive substring/prefix matching instead of properly tokenizing comma-separated auth-params (respecting quoted values and backslash escapes), which could produce false matches on parameter names. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both implement an equivalent quote-aware, escape-aware comma-splitting state machine, but #3041 splits the entire header into segments and then locates the Bearer challenge via per-segment scheme detection (_extract_bearer_auth_params), so it correctly isolates params when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic ..., Bearer ...'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips text before the header's first space and treats everything after as one challenge's params, which would misparse multi-challenge headers.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 is a minimal, self-contained fix directly in the existing 'attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS' branch: it reuses existing JSONRPCError/ErrorData plumbing and correlates the error to the specific pending request id, so the exact caller awaiting that request unblocks with a standard JSON-RPC error. #3098's diff bundles an unrelated stylistic change (dropping the `_annotations` alias from `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations`) alongside a new generic ExceptionGroup-unwrapping helper whose call site isn't shown in this diff, making its actual coverage of the hang scenario harder to verify from the change alone.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the failure path of _handle_reconnection() for the SSE reconnection logic in streamable_http.py: when reconnection to resume the stream ultimately fails, the waiting caller currently gets nothing (a silent hang) or an opaque/wrong exception instead of a clear, actionable error. #2395 fixes this by detecting the 'max attempts exceeded' branch and pushing an explicit JSONRPCError (matched to the original request id) through read_stream_writer. #3098 fixes it by adding a recursive _unwrap_exception() helper that digs a StreamableHTTPError out of anyio's ExceptionGroup wrapping so the correct exception type propagates on reconnection failure. Same trigger (reconnection failing) and same goal (caller must learn about the failure instead of hanging/getting a useless error) via two different mechanisms (in-band JSON-RPC error vs. raised exception). (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #2962's test/comment cites SEP-1577 and issue #2960 as the spec basis: tool_result blocks must be preceded by tool_use, but tool_use carries no requirement to be followed by tool_result, so no-raise is the spec-conformant behavior. #3053 only improves the error message while preserving the raise, which contradicts that cited spec requirement, so it should be closed in favor of #2962.

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same branch in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) governing what happens when a previous assistant tool_use is not followed by a matching tool_result — but they resolve it in opposite directions. #2962 adds `has_tool_results` to the guard so the id-matching check is skipped entirely when there are no tool_results, meaning a tool_use with no following tool_result no longer raises at all. #3053 keeps the raise but adds a dedicated `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` branch with a clearer message, so a tool_use with no following tool_result still raises (just with better wording) — the reverse of #2962's outcome. They cannot both be applied as intended: whichever merges second either re-breaks the other's fix or sits as dead code on top of it. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both implement an equivalent quote-aware, escape-aware comma-splitting state machine, but #3041 splits the entire header into segments and then locates the Bearer challenge via per-segment scheme detection (_extract_bearer_auth_params), so it correctly isolates params when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic ..., Bearer ...'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips text before the header's first space and treats everything after as one challenge's params, which would misparse multi-challenge headers.
